ITQAN:v2p549/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p549/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p549/r6.claim: A pronoun attached to one referent may switch to another: “him” after creating the human from clay refers to Adam's descendant, since Adam was not made from a sperm-drop.
ITQAN:v2p549/r6.anchor: وقد يجيء الضمير متصلا بشيء وهو لغيره نحو ﴿ ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من سلالة من طين ﴾ يعني آدم ثم قال ﴿ ثم جعلناه نطفة ﴾

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r3.claim: It recounts human development from clay through a blood clot to another creation, recalling 22:5.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r3.anchor: reminiscent of 22:5, recounts a human being’s development starting from a clot of blood and culminating in another creation (vv. 12–14)

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r3.claim: The creation sequence in al-Mu’minūn describes the same reality as this passage and summarizes the stages that testify to resurrection.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r3.anchor: The following verses of Sūrah al-Mu’minūn point to precisely the same reality:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r1.claim: Qarār is the place of settlement, here the womb; makīn describes its stability or the secure position of whoever occupies it, metaphorically like a road one travels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p551/r1.anchor: والقرار مكان الاستقرار والمراد هنا الرحم

BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r1.claim: “Then We made him” refers to humankind as a species through individuals distinct from Adam.

BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r2.claim: Some say “him” means Adam’s offspring, with an omitted possessive; Adam himself was made from the extract of clay.
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ثم جعلناه أي نسله فحذف المضاف فيكون المراد بالإنسان آدم

BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r3.claim: Nuṭfa means clear, pure water and is also used for a man’s semen; God created the human from it.
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r3.anchor: بأن خلقناه منها والنطفة الماء الصافي ويعبر بها عن ماء الرجل

BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r4.claim: Qarār is a stable resting place, meaning the womb; the verbal noun is used emphatically.
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r4.anchor: أي مستقر وهو الرحم عبر عنها بالقرار الذي هو مصدر مبالغة

BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r5.claim: Makīn means secure or fortified, describing the womb by the quality of what rests inside it.
BURSEVI:v6p50#2/r5.anchor: أي حصين وهو وصف لها بصفة ما استقر فيها

RAZI-FULL:v23p74/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p74/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p74/r2.claim: Human development is presented as one of several proofs, proceeding through nine stages of creation.
RAZI-FULL:v23p74/r2.anchor: الاستدلال يتقلب الإنسان في أدوار الخلقة وأكوان الفطرة وهي تسعة

RAZI-FULL:v23p74/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p74/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p74/r9.claim: God first created human substance from clay, then made it semen in the fathers’ loins and conveyed it through intercourse into the woman’s womb.
RAZI-FULL:v23p74/r9.anchor: ومعنى جعل الإنسان نطفة أنه خلق

RAZI-FULL:v23p74/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p74/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p74/r10.claim: Qarār denotes the place where something settles; the womb is called by the verbal noun for its settled location and is described as secure.
RAZI-FULL:v23p74/r10.anchor: والمراد بالقرار موضع القرار وهو المستقر فسماه بالمصدر ثم وصف الرحم بالمكانة

RAZI-FULL:v23p74/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p74/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p74/r11.claim: Rāzī gives two explanations of the womb’s being makīn: the description may transfer from what is settled there, or refer to the womb’s own secure, protected position.
RAZI-FULL:v23p74/r11.anchor: كقولك طريق سائر أو لمكانتها في نفسها لأنها تمكنت من حيث هي وأحرزت

STUDYQURAN:23:13/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:13/r1.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:23:13/r1.anchor: The drop refers to seminal fluid

STUDYQURAN:23:13/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:13/r2.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:23:13/r2.claim: The secure dwelling place is the womb.
STUDYQURAN:23:13/r2.anchor: the secure dwelling place is the womb (R, Ṭ).

TABATABAI:23:12-14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r1.claim: After describing believers' virtues, the passage explains human creation and provision to show that God alone is Lord of humanity and all things and alone deserves worship.
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r1.anchor: عقبه بشرح خلقهم وخلق ما أنعم عليهم من النعم مقرونا بتدبير أمرهم

TABATABAI:23:12-14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r3.claim: “The human” denotes the human kind, including Adam and his descendants: Adam was first formed from clay, then his offspring from a drop, as in 32:7–8; readings limited to Adam's descendants or to Adam alone are rejected.
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r3.anchor: وظاهر السياق أن المراد بالإنسان هو النوع فيشمل آدم ومن دونه

TABATABAI:23:12-14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r4.claim: If “human” meant only Adam's descendants and their clay origin meant semen ultimately comes from earth, the next clause should say “then We created him as a drop,” paralleling the subsequent stages.
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r4.anchor: لكان الظاهر أن يقال ثم خلقناه نطفة كما قيل ثم خلقنا النطفة علقة

TABATABAI:23:12-14/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r6.claim: Nuṭfa means a little water, sometimes water generally; qarār, literally a verbal noun, emphatically means the place of settlement—the womb—and makīn describes its secure holding of the drop or the drop's secure position.
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r6.anchor: النطفة القليل من الماء وربما يطلق على مطلق الماء

TABATABAI:23:12-14/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r7.claim: The stages show a change in the mode of creation: God first formed the human from clay, then made him a drop securely settled in the womb.
TABATABAI:23:12-14/r7.anchor: أي بدلنا طريق خلقه من هذا إلى ذاك

TABATABAI:23:13-14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r1.claim: The pronoun in “We brought him into being” refers to the human whose bones had been clothed with flesh; he is transformed from dead, ignorant, powerless matter into a living, knowing, capable being.

TABATABAI:23:13-14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r4.claim: One grammatical account uses thumma for stages separated by a complete break, while fa marks the closer succession of clot-to-morsel, morsel-to-bones, and bones-to-flesh.
TABATABAI:23:13-14/r4.anchor: وقد قيل في وجهه أن ما عطف بثم له بينونة كاملة مع ما عطف عليه

TABRISI:23:12-19/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:12-19/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:12-19/r11.claim: The account contradicts al-Naẓẓām’s view that the human being is a spirit and Maʿmar’s view that a human is an indivisible, nonbodily thing.
TABRISI:23:12-19/r11.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على فساد قول النظام في أن الإنسان هو الروح وقول معمر إن الإنسان شيء لا ينقسم وإنه ليس بجسم

THALABI:v7p41#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p41#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p41#2/r3.claim: The drop remains in a secure place, the womb, until it reaches its appointed term.
THALABI:v7p41#2/r3.anchor: ثم جعلناه نطفة في قرار مكين حريز مكين لاستقرارها فيه إلى بلوغ أمدها وهو الرحم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p537#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p537#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p537#2/r1.claim: The human is Adam's descendant, since Adam himself was not a drop in a womb.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p537#2/r1.anchor: يعني ابن آدم؛ لأن آدم لم يكن نطفة في رحم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p537#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p537#2/r2.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p537#2/r2.claim: On the first interpretation, the pronoun shifts to Adam's descendant rather than directly referring to the human named earlier; context licenses this inference.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p537#2/r2.anchor: وعلى القول الأول عادت الكناية إلى ابن آدم لا إلى الإنسان المذكور في الآية الأولى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p537#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p537#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p537#2/r3.claim: The contextual pronoun shift is compared with 5:101, where the pronoun refers to similar questions other than those just mentioned.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p537#2/r3.anchor: لا تسألوا عن أشياء إن تبد لكم تسؤكم وإن تسألوا عنها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538/r1.claim: Qarār means a settled place or residence, named with a verbal noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538/r1.anchor: يعني مستقر، وموضع قرار، فسماه بالمصدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538/r2.speaker: المفضل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538/r2.claim: Makin means firmly settled, not unstable.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538/r3.claim: The secure place is the womb, prepared to hold the embryo until its appointed term.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p538/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس والمفسرون في قوله: {مكين}: يريد الرحم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r7.claim: The human is made a drop at the beginning of his formation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r7.anchor: { ثم جعلناه } جعلنا الإنسان { نطفة } في أول بدو خلقه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r8.claim: The secure resting place is the womb.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r8.anchor: في قرار مكين } يعني: الرحم. وقوله:

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r3.claim: The secure resting place is the womb.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p394/r3.anchor: قوله: {ثم جعلناه نطفة في قرار مكين} [المؤمنون: 13] الرحم.

ELMALILI:23:12-16/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16/r22.claim: He takes “him” as either humankind or its progeny and explains the verse as making the human a nutfa settled in the firm resting place of the womb.
ELMALILI:23:12-16/r22.anchor: bir karâr-ı mekînde bir nutfe kıldık yani o insan cinsini veya neslini mekânetli bir karargâh olan rahimde temekkün eder bir nutfe yaptık.

ELMALILI:23:12-16/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16/r23.claim: The first clay-created human is followed by reproduction through a nutfa, a lowly fluid extract, as stated in al-Sajda 32:8.
ELMALILI:23:12-16/r23.anchor: mantûkunca hakir bir su sülâlesi olan nutfeden tenâsül tarîkiyle yaratılarak diğer bir sülâle oldu.

ELMALILI:23:12-16/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16/r24.claim: In Qur'anic usage nutfa is more specifically the seed within semen, not semen itself, because the thing that settles in the womb is the seed.
ELMALILI:23:12-16/r24.anchor: “nutfe” yalnız meninin ismi değil, daha ziyade meni içindeki tohumunun ismidir.

ELMALILI:23:12-16/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16/r25.claim: An alternative allows the pronoun in jaʿalnāhu to refer to sulāla in the sense of something extracted: God made that clay extract into a nutfa.
ELMALILI:23:12-16/r25.anchor: zamirinin meslûl mânasıyla “sülâle”ye ircâ‘ı da tecviz edilmiştir ki o çamur sülâlesini nutfe yaptık demek olur.

ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r1.claim: Once the nutfa stage is reached, human creation follows its customary natural course; the original creation of clay, sulāla, and the first human or nutfa was beyond nature because neither humans nor their nature yet existed.
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r1.anchor: İşte nutfe yapıldıktan sonra insan hilkati tabî‘î ve kānûnî denilen mu‘tad şeklini almış oldu.

ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r2.claim: The creating power is distinct from human nature: nature belongs to the thing itself and cannot be the external cause of its own change.
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r2.anchor: Demek ki insanı yaratan kudret-i hâlıka insan tabiatından başkadır. Her hangi bir şeyin tabiatı ise o şeyin kendisinden hâriç olamaz.

ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r3.claim: Nature is considered regular and unchanging; a change in a thing's nature entails change in the thing itself and therefore calls for an external influence.
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r3.anchor: Onun için tabiat ancak muttarid ve lâyetegayyer olmak üzere mülâhaza edilebilir. Ve bir şey kendisi değişmedikçe tabiatının değişmesine imkân tasavvur olunamaz.

ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r4.claim: Natural sciences seek an external cause for every observed transformation rather than allowing nature to change by itself; thus the transformations point beyond nature.
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r4.anchor: “Ulûm-i tabî‘iye” nâmı verilen ilimlerin hiçbiri yoktur ki mütalaa ettiği bir tehavvülün ayrı bir sebebini aramasın

ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r5.claim: Nature can undergo selection and development, but the Creator, who rules over natures, causes them; if nature ruled itself, clay and nutfa could not develop into later forms.
ELMALILI:23:12-16#2/r5.anchor: Lâkin o ıstıfâ ve tekâmülü yapan tabiat değil, tabiatlar üzerinde hâkim olan Hâlık’tır.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r15.claim: Although the fluid is technically the second stage in the sequence described in 23:13, it is the clearest and nearest starting point for reflection and is often foregrounded in Qur'anic accounts.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r15.anchor: Fakat fi’l-hâl nazar yürütülmek için en zâhir ve en yakın olan mebde’ bu olduğu cihetle ekser âyetlerde evvelâ bu mebde’e nazar-ı dikkat celbolunmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r1.claim: Although the creation verbs are past tense in Arabic, the author renders them in the present because the process of each person's creation continues.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r1.anchor: Bu bölümde geçen “yaratıyoruz, getiriyoruz” gibi fiillerin asılları âyetlerin metninde geçmiş zamanlıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r2.claim: Qur'anic past-tense forms can serve, among other purposes, to emphasize that the reported information is certain.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r2.anchor: Kur’an’da verilen bilginin kesinliğine işaret etmek gibi bazı sebeplerle şimdiki, gelecek veya geniş zaman yerine geçmiş zaman fiilinin kullanıldığı bilinmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r5.claim: After sperm fertilizes the ovum in the woman's reproductive tract, the zygote, called nutfa at this stage, reaches the womb described as a secure refuge.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r5.anchor: Nutfe ile bu aşamadaki döllenmiş hücre (zigot) kastedilmektedir. Bu hücrelerin bazı uzantılar çıkararak rahim iç zarına

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r8.claim: The passage summarizes each person's biological formation from soil-derived food and plant growth through gestation to a fully formed body.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r8.anchor: topraktan, dolayısıyla toprakta beslenip büyüyen bitkilerden alınan besin aşamasından başlayarak ana karnında ete kemiğe bürünmesine

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r10.claim: By recalling these gifts, the verses implicitly call people to recognize their Creator and fulfill their debt of gratitude.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:12/r10.anchor: Âyette Allah’ın insanoğluna bütün bu ihsanları hatırlatılmakta ve dolaylı olarak ondan yaratıcısını tanıyıp şükran borcunu yerine getirmesi istenmektedir

QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r9.claim: From a uniform drop, God differentiates flesh, bone, hair, nails, nerves, skin, brain, and veins, assigning each member its form and each part its known condition.
QUSHAYRI:v2p336/r9.anchor: قطرة أجزاؤها متماثلة ، ونطفة أبعاضها متشاكلة ، ثم جعل بعضها لحما وبعضها عظما

BURHAN:v4p32/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p32/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p32/r7.claim: The pronoun in then We made him a drop attaches to the human but refers to his offspring, since Adam was not created from a drop.
BURHAN:v4p32/r7.anchor: فهذا لولده لأن آدم لم يخلق من نطفة

ITQAN:v3p227#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p227#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p227#2/r3.claim: In the clearest example, الإنسان first means Adam, while the pronoun in ثم جعلناه refers to his offspring.
ITQAN:v3p227#2/r3.anchor: فإن المراد به آدم ثم أعاد عليه الضمير مرادا به ولده

SAMIN-DURR:23:13/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:13/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:13/r1.claim: The pronoun may refer to a human other than Adam, with an omitted possessive, or to Adam with his descendants intended; it may also refer to humanity as suited to descendants.
SAMIN-DURR:23:13/r1.anchor: فإن أريد غير آدم فواضح، ويكون خلقه من سلالة الطين خلق أصله وهو آدم

SAMIN-DURR:23:13/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:13/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:23:13/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī favors reading al-insān as apt to refer either to the origin or descendants, with each pronoun referring to what suits it.
SAMIN-DURR:23:13/r2.anchor: ويعود كل شيء لما يليق به. وإليه نحا الزمخشري

SAMIN-DURR:23:13/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:13/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:13/r3.claim: The phrase may attach to jaʿalnāhu or be an omitted adjective of nuṭfah.
SAMIN-DURR:23:13/r3.anchor: يجوز أن يتعلق بالجعل، وأن يتعلق بمحذوف

SAMIN-DURR:23:13/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:13/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:13/r4.claim: Qarār is a place of settlement, here the womb; makīn describes its secure location, metaphorically like a road called travelling, or because it is firmly established in itself.
SAMIN-DURR:23:13/r4.anchor: والقرار: المستقر وهو موضع الاستقرار. والمراد بها الرحم

ZAJJAJ:v4p8/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p8/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p8/r4.claim: On the preceding interpretation, جعلناه refers to Adam's descendant.
ZAJJAJ:v4p8/r4.anchor: على هذا القول يعني ولد آدم

ZAJJAJ:v4p8/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p8/r5.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p8/r5.claim: An alternative says the clay-derived سلالة is Adam's semen.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p603/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p603/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p603/r1.claim: Emphasis depends on context: al-Mu’minūn mentions death more often and foregrounds human creation, so creation receives two emphases and resurrection one, since resurrection is easier than originating life; both are easy for God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p603/r1.anchor: فلهذا جعل سبحانه وتعالى توكيدين في الخلق وتوكيداً واحداً في البعث لأن البعث أهون عليه من الخلق من عدم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p3/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p3/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p3/r1.claim: He says the Qur’anic account of embryonic stages matches knowledge reached only in the modern era, which specialists in anatomy and medicine describe as scientifically precise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p3/r1.anchor: مما لم يكن معروفاً قبل هذا العصر

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r12.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r12.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r12.claim: The preceding believers' glad tidings and the warnings implicit for faithless disbelievers are realities, though deniers of resurrection and the hereafter dismiss them as fantasy and mock them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r12.anchor: The glad tidings given to the believers in the previous section are a definite reality. Similarly, the warnings they conceal for the disbelievers devoid of faith are also a definite reality.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r1.claim: People who reject resurrection and the hereafter treat the promised realities as imaginary and make fun of them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r1.anchor: By presenting the objections of such people, attention is directed to the signs in their inside and outside world.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r2.claim: Reflection on the stages of human creation makes clear that the God who created people can readily recreate those who die and decay into dust.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r2.anchor: if a person only reflects on the phases of his creation it will become crystal clear that the God Who is capable of doing all this can have no difficulty in re-creating those who die and decay into dust.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r4.claim: The resurrection argument also appears in 22:5; this passage develops it further and elaborates aspects not treated there.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p244/r4.anchor: This argument has also been stated in verse 5 of S ūrah al-Ḥajj.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r1.claim: Islahi connects the creation stages here with 22:5: there they prove resurrection, and “so that We make evident for you” signals that the gradual sequence displays God's power and wisdom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r1.anchor: There, the opening words were: ﺐٍ رَﻳۡ ﺘﻢۡ /.ۡ ﻛﻨۡ نۡ ﻣ	ﻦَ  ﻟۡﺒَﻌۡﺚ if you are in any doubt of being raised to life again

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r2.claim: The stages of human development are familiar, and modern science has disclosed aspects the Qur'an only hinted at; further knowledge reveals more of these secrets.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r2.anchor: the more knowledge human beings gain, the more they know of these secrets.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r3.claim: A drop arising from clay is gradually nourished until it becomes people such as Socrates, Hippocrates, Aristotle, and Galen, prompting reflection on whether this elaborate process is accidental.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r3.anchor: ultimately, the likes of Socrates, Hippocrates, Aristotle and Galen are created. The question is: Is all this happening of its own accord?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r4.claim: The sequence of creation, its care, and its evident power and wisdom cannot be meaningless products of uncontrolled matter; the One who forms a human from a drop can recreate that person.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p245/r4.anchor: Is all this power, wisdom, providence and affection a meaningless thing which has no purpose and fate? Is the being Who fashions out a human being from a drop of fluid unable to create him again?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r1.claim: The Qur'an directs people to inspect their own bodies and stages of development; reflection there supplies the answers without searching far afield.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p246/r1.anchor: If they reflect on their own phases of creation, they will get all the answers.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r1.claim: If “human” first means humankind as a species, the pronoun refers to its individual descendants other than Adam; proposed antecedents involving an unstated son of Adam or omitted possessive are possible but strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r1.anchor: الضمير في قوله تعالى ( ثم جعلناه نطفة ( عائد على الجنس باعتبار أفراده المغايرة لآدم عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r2.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r2.claim: Al-Baḥr suggests that if “human” first means Adam, the pronoun refers to his son, an unmentioned antecedent made clear by its familiarity; the author finds this unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r2.anchor: وإذا أريد بالإنسان أولا آدم عليه السلام فالضمير على ما في البحر عائد على غير مذكور

ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r3.claim: Other analyses supply “offspring” after human, use Adam for his descendants, or make the pronoun refer to the extracted substance, understood as the extracted one or as water; the last means making the extract into a sperm-drop.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r3.anchor: أو على الإنسان والكلام على حذف مضاف أي ثم جعلنا نسله وقيل يراد بالإنسان أولا آدم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r4.claim: Most analyses treat nuṭfa as the second object of jaʿala in the sense “make”; another analysis takes jaʿala as “create,” with nuṭfa accusative after an omitted preposition, a choice favored by some investigators.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r4.anchor: في سائر الوجوه مفعولا ثانيا للجعل على أنه بمعنى التصيير

ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r5.claim: Qarār originally means stable remaining, a verbal noun used intensively as a place; here it means the womb.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r5.anchor: أي مستقر وهو في الأصل مصدر من قر يقر قرارا بمعنى ثبت ثبوتا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r6.claim: Makin means securely situated; applied to the sperm-drop it is metaphorical, or it describes the womb as fixed and retaining its contents, implying that the drop is guarded and protected.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p13/r6.anchor: أي متمكن مع أن التمكن وصف ذي المكان وهو النطفة هنا على سبيل المجاز

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p411#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p411#3/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p411#3/r5.claim: The human being is made into a sperm-drop.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p411#3/r5.anchor: يعني الذي هو الإنسان جعلناه نطفة، {في قرار مكين} حريز،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p411#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p411#3/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p411#3/r6.claim: The secure resting place is the womb, prepared to hold the drop until its term is complete.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p411#3/r6.anchor: حريز، وهو الرحم مكن [أي قد هيئ] (4) لاستقرارها فيه إلى بلوغ أمدها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r1.claim: “Then We made him a drop” means We made his offspring a drop, with the annexed noun omitted; alternatively, We made the extract a drop. The masculine pronoun treats it as a substance, extracted thing, or water.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r1.anchor: ثم جعلنه } ثم جعلنا نسله فحذف المضاف.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r2.claim: The secure resting place is the womb; makīn originally describes the resting place but is applied emphatically to its location.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:13-14/r2.anchor: مستقر حصين يعني الرحم، وهو في الأصل صفة للمستقر وصف به المحل للمبالغة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r2.claim: After mentioning Paradise, the sūra proves resurrection through the first creation, moves to the greater created cosmos, then warns through earlier peoples, turns to gratitude for human distinction, and returns to proofs of resurrection and divine oneness.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r2.anchor: استدل على القدرة عليه بابتداء الخلق للإنسان , ثم لما هو أكبر منه من الأكوان

BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r3.claim: The narrative begins with Noah because he was the first prophet and his ark rescue recalls that humanity descends from him; after warnings and blessings, the next sūra continues the preceding discussion of guarding sexual integrity.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r3.anchor: وابتدأ بقصة نوح عليه الصلاة والسلام لأنه أول , ولأن نجاته كانت في الفلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines creation as measuring out components that will appear as a form after mixture and composition; Biqāʿī applies this to clay's mixture and the unexpected emergence of a human.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r6.anchor: لأن الخلق - كما مر عن الحرالي في أول البقرة : تقدير أمشاج ما يراد إظهاره بعد الامتزاج والتركيب صورة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r7.claim: The water is the second, purer origin of humanity and the source of living things; jaʿala describes bringing about a result through a cause, while thumma marks the striking transition from clay to water.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r7.anchor: أتبعه سبحانه أصله الثاني الذي هو أطهر الطهورين : الماء

BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r8.claim: The pronoun may refer to the clay itself or to the human kind extracted from clay and developed through its successive individuals.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r8.anchor: هذا النوع المسلول من المخلوق من الطين بتطوير أفراده ببديع الصنع

BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r9.claim: The drop is a flowing fluid with no trace of clay remaining.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r9.anchor: نطفة } أي ماء دافقا لا أثر للطين فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r10.claim: Qarār is originally a verbal noun used as the name of a place; the secure receptacle comprises the loins and ribs, then the womb, and is protected from corrupting influences.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p186#2/r10.anchor: في قرار } أي من الصلب والترائب ثم الرحم , مصدر جعل اسما للموضع { مكين * } أي مانع من الأشياء المفسدة

DURR-FULL:v6p90/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r5.claim: Qatada says Adam was extracted from clay, while his descendants were created from humble fluid.
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في الآية قال: استل آدم من طين وخلقت ذريته من ماء مهين

DURR-FULL:v6p90/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r6.claim: Ibn Masud says the embryo's fluid spreads through every hair and nail, remains forty days, then settles in the womb and becomes a clot.
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: إن النطفة إذا وقعت في الرحم طارت في كل شعر وظفر فتمكث أربعين يوما

DURR-FULL:v6p90/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r7.claim: A weak-chain report attributed to the Prophet through Ibn Abbas says the limbs and veins tremble when the generative fluid exits and falls into the womb.
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس مرفوعا النطفة التي يخلق منها الولد ترعد لها الأعضاء والعروق كلها إذا خرجت

DURR-FULL:v6p90/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r9.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r9.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib calls coitus interruptus concealed infanticide.
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r9.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب أنه سئل عن عزل النساء فقال: ذلك الوأد الخفي

DURR-FULL:v6p90/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r10.claim: Ibn Masud likewise calls coitus interruptus hidden infanticide.
DURR-FULL:v6p90/r10.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال في العزل: هي الموؤدة الخفية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r1.claim: The passage starts a new argument after the account of believers: God alone creates, human beings belong to Him, and human creation and other creatures display divine power and favor, refuting the polytheists’ central error and contrasting grateful believers with ungrateful idolaters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r1.anchor: وهذا شروع في الاستدلال على انفراد الله تعالى بالخلق وبعظيم القدرة التي لا يشاركه فيها غيره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r2.claim: The oath lām and emphatic particle address polytheists as if they denied the report, because they do not act on what they know.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r2.anchor: وتأكيد الخبر بلام القسم وحرف التحقيق مراعى فيه التعريض بالمشركين المنزلين منزلة من ينكر هذا الخبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r3.claim: Creation means bringing into being and making, as in the cited verse about God creating what He wills.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r3.anchor: الإنشاء والصنع ، وقد تقدم في قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas takes al-insān as the human species, with the definite article used generically; the pronoun in jaʿalnāhu returns to humankind.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r4.anchor: وفسر به ابن عباس ومجاهد ، فالتعريف للجنس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r5.claim: Mujahid likewise understands al-insān as humankind in general, rather than one individual.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r5.anchor: وفسر به ابن عباس ومجاهد ، فالتعريف للجنس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r6.claim: Sulāla is something drawn out from another thing, like a sword pulled from its sheath; the pattern suggests a small quantity, as in qalamāma and ṣubāba.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r6.anchor: والسلالة : الشيء المسلول ، أي المنتزع من شيء آخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r7.claim: The preposition min marks origin: the human was formed from an extracted substance, understood as the combined reproductive material of male and female.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r7.anchor: و { من } ابتدائية ، أي خلقناه منفصلا وآتيا من سلالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r8.claim: The author describes the extract as nourishment converted into blood, male blood producing stored fatty material in the testes that becomes semen, while female blood leaves ova in the uterine channel; their union forms an embryo, ultimately from earth-derived food.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p21/r8.anchor: وهذه السلالة هي ما يفرزه جهاز الهضم من الغذاء حين يصير دما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r1.claim: The next stage is the union of the two extracts in the womb; the male extract is called a drop because it drips into the womb through its channel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r1.anchor: سميت سلالة الذكر نطفة لأنها تنطف ، أي تقطر في الرحم في قناة معروفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r2.claim: Nuṭfa is accusative as a circumstantial expression, while in a firm lodging is the second object of jaʿalnāhu; thumma marks elevated rank because placement there is more remarkable.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r2.anchor: منصوب على الحال وقوله : { في قرار مكين } هو المفعول الثاني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r3.claim: The pronoun refers to the human as derived from the extract; the sense is that God places the reproductive substance in a secure lodging, so the verse uses jaʿala with fī for placing rather than khalq.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r3.anchor: فضمير { جعلناه } عائد إلى الإنسان باعتبار أنه من السلالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r4.claim: Qarār is originally the verbal noun of settling but here names the place; makīn means firmly fixed, applied to the place by a rational metaphor that emphasizes its secure condition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r4.anchor: والقرار في الأصل : مصدر قر إذا ثبت في مكانه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r5.claim: The account recalls the verses describing creation from earth and then from a drop.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r5.anchor: وقد تقدم قوله تعالى : { أكفرت بالذي خلقك من تراب ثم من نطفة }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r6.claim: Qatada allows al-insān to mean Adam: the sulāla is the specially selected clay from which Adam was formed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r6.anchor: وقال بذلك قتادة فتكون السلالة الطينة الخاصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r7.claim: On Qatada’s reading, the pronoun returns to Adam as ancestor of his descendants, an instance of shifting the referent, and the sense matches the statement about Adam’s offspring.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p22/r7.anchor: وعليه فضمير { جعلناه نطفة } على هذا الوجه عائد إلى الإنسان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r2.speaker: قتادة وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r2.claim: Qatada and others take the human as Adam, extracted from clay; verse 13's pronoun then refers to Adam's son, understood despite not being named.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r2.anchor: واختلف المفسرون في قوله الإنسان فقال قتادة وغيره: أراد آدم عليه السلام لأنه استل من الطين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r9.claim: Nutfa can mean either a little or a great quantity of water; here it means Adam's son's semen.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r9.anchor: تقع في اللغة على قليل الماء وعلى كثيره، وهي هنا لمني ابن آدم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r10.claim: The secure abode is the woman's womb, a firmly situated resting place for the child.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#3/r10.anchor: من المرأة هو موضع الولد، و «المكين» المتمكن فكأن القرار هو المتمكن في الرحم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p462#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p462#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p462#2/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to Adam's descendant, made a drop of semen in the womb.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p462#2/r1.anchor: ثم جعلناه يعني ابن آدم نطفة في قرار وهو الرحم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p462#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p462#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p462#2/r2.claim: Qarār makīn is the womb, a secure place prepared for the embryo to settle; the terms nuṭfa, ʿalaqa, and muḍgha were explained at 22:5.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p462#2/r2.anchor: في قرار وهو الرحم مكين أي حريز قد هيىء لاستقراره فيه وقد شرحنا في سورة الحج 5 معنى النطفة والعلقة والمضغة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p466/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p466/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p466/r1.claim: The pronoun in then We made him a drop refers to humankind as a species, as in the verse saying humanity began from clay and its offspring from a weak fluid.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p466/r1.anchor: هذا الضمير عائد على جنس الإنسان، كما قال في الآية الأخرى: {وبدأ خلق الإنسان من طين * ثم جعل نسله من سلالة من ماء مهين}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p466/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p466/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p466/r2.claim: The cited phrase māʾ mahīn means weak fluid.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p466/r2.anchor: أي: ضعيف، كما قال: {ألم نخلقكم من ماء مهين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p466/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p466/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p466/r3.claim: The secure place is the womb, prepared to receive the fluid until its appointed term and measured duration, as it develops through successive states.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p466/r3.anchor: يعني: الرحم معد لذلك مهيأ له، {إلى قدر معلوم * فقدرنا فنعم القادرون}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p466#2/r15.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p466#2/r15.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p466#2/r15.claim: The Prophet says a person develops as a drop, then a clot, then a morsel, each for forty days; an angel then breathes the spirit and records provision, lifespan, deeds, and whether the person is blessed or wretched, while final destiny can differ from the apparent course of deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p466#2/r15.anchor: عن عبد الله -هو ابن مسعود-قال: حدثنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهو الصادق المصدوق: "إن أحدكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r1.claim: The preceding Ibn Masud hadith is also reported by both Sahih collections through Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A'mash.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r1.anchor: أخرجاه من حديث سليمان بن مهران الأعمش

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود عن خيثمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says the drop spreads through every hair and nail after entering the womb, remains forty days, then descends and becomes a clot.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r2.anchor: عن خيثمة قال: قال عبد الله (8) -يعني: ابن مسعود-إن النطفة إذا وقعت في الرحم، طارت في كل شعر وظفر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r3.speaker: عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r3.claim: In answer to a Jewish man's question, the Prophet says humans are formed from both male and female fluid: the man's thick fluid produces bones and sinews, and the woman's thin fluid produces flesh and blood; the Jew says earlier prophets taught the same.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: مر يهودي برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يحدث أصحابه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r4.speaker: حذيفة بن أسيد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r4.claim: The Prophet says an angel enters the womb after the drop has settled for forty nights and records sex, blessedness or wretchedness, deeds, effects, misfortunes, and provision; the record is then sealed without additions or subtractions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r4.anchor: حذيفة بن أسيد الغفاري قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r5.speaker: أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r5.claim: Anas reports that an angel assigned to the womb successively reports a drop, clot, and morsel; if God wills to create it, the angel asks and records sex, blessedness, wretchedness, provision, and lifespan in the mother's womb.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p467/r5.anchor: عن أنس؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

JISHUMI:v7p5026/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5026/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5026/r9.claim: Nutfa means a man’s semen, though Arabs use it for both a little and a large body of water.
JISHUMI:v7p5026/r9.anchor: والنطفة: ماء الرجل، والعرب تقول للماء القليل: نطفة، وللماء الكثير: نطفة

JISHUMI:v7p5026/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5026/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5026/r10.claim: A hadith describes a rider between two seas without fearing danger; the phrase means the eastern and western seas.
JISHUMI:v7p5026/r10.anchor: ومنه الحديث: حتى يسير الراكب بين النطفتين لا يخشى جورا، يعني بين بحر المشرق وبحر المغرب

JISHUMI:v7p5026/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5026/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5026/r11.claim: The root نطف refers to drops; نطف means to drip, and a نطوف night has continuous rain.
JISHUMI:v7p5026/r11.anchor: والنطف: القطر، نطف ينطف، وليلة نطوف دائمة القطر

JISHUMI:v7p5028/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5028/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5028/r4.claim: One account links the creation passage to prior afterlife blessings, turning to blessings at human origins and prompting reflection.
JISHUMI:v7p5028/r4.anchor: لما ذكر نعمه على المؤمنين بما أعد لهم في الآخرة ابتدأ بذكر نعمه عليه ابتداء، ومنبها له على النظر في نعمه

JISHUMI:v7p5028/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5028/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5028/r10.claim: Then God made the human, meaning Adam’s descendants, a drop of semen.
JISHUMI:v7p5028/r10.anchor: ثم جعلناه أي: جعلنا الإنسان، وهم ذرية آدم نطفة وهو المني

JISHUMI:v7p5028/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5028/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5028/r11.claim: A suitable place is prepared for semen to settle; makīn may mean protected, namely the womb.
JISHUMI:v7p5028/r11.anchor: في قرار مكين أي: مكن لذلك بأن هيأ لاستقراره، وقيل: مكين: حريز، وهو الرحم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p48/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p48/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p48/r1.claim: Nutfah specifically means the male fluid from which a child forms by adhering.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p48/r1.anchor: النطفة هي ماء الذكر الذي يعلق منه الولد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p48/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p48/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p48/r2.claim: Nutfah can also be used for any water.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p48/r2.anchor: وقد ينطلق اسم النطفة على كل ماء

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p48/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p48/r3.speaker: بعض شعراء هذيل
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p48/r3.claim: A Hudhayl poet uses nutf for water in a line about thirsty drinkers, supporting the broader sense.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p48/r3.anchor: وأنهما لحرابا حروب … وشرابان بالنطف الظوامي

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p48/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p48/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p48/r4.claim: The secure, well-prepared place is the womb, made suitable for the embryo to settle there.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p48/r4.anchor: بالقرار الرحم , ومكين : أي متمكن قد هيىء لاستقراره

MUQATIL:23:12-14/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:12-14/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:12-14/r3.claim: The drop of fluid is Adam’s progeny.

MUQATIL:23:12-14/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:12-14/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:12-14/r4.claim: The secure lodging is the womb, where the drop is established.
MUQATIL:23:12-14/r4.anchor: يعنى الرحم: تمكن النطفة فى الرحم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r1.claim: Then We made him means his offspring, with the annexed noun omitted and its dependent taking its place; Adam himself did not become a drop of semen.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r1.anchor: أى نسله فحذف المضاف وأقيم المضاف إليه مقامه لأن آدم عليه السلام لم يصر نطفة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r2.claim: Nasafi compares the wording to the account that human creation began from clay and then Adam's offspring came from a fluid extract.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r2.anchor: وهو كقوله وبدأ خلق الإنسان من طين ثم جعل نسله من سلالة من ماء مهين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r3.claim: Another view takes the human to mean Adam's children and the extract to mean semen, which Arabs call sulala; it is extracted from clay in the sense of being from Adam, who was made from clay.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r3.anchor: وقيل الإنسان بنو آدم والسلالة النطفة والعرب تسمى النطفة سلالة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r4.claim: Nutfa means a small amount of water.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r5.claim: Qarar is a place of rest, namely the womb; makin means secure or fortified.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#7/r5.anchor: ﴿ في قرار ﴾ مستقر يعنى الرحم ﴿ مكين ﴾ حصين

QURTUBI-FULL:23:12-13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:12-13/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:12-13/r2.claim: The pronoun refers to Adam’s descendant, omitted because the context is familiar and no other meaning fits; Qurtubi compares 38:32.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:12-13/r2.anchor: وإن كان لم يذكر لشهرة الأمر فإن المعنى لا يصلح إلا له

QURTUBI-FULL:23:12-14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:12-14/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:12-14/r3.claim: Qurtubi refers meanings and legal rulings about the drop, clot, and morsel to his earlier commentary on Sūrat al-Ḥajj.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:12-14/r3.anchor: قد مضى القول في النطفة والعلقة والمضغة وما في ذلك من الأحكام في أول الحج
